InsightLegi Explorer

Use this explorer to look up a state's laws and see whether a law involves money, where the law directs that money, and what the receiving fund reported in the state's own financial statements each year. Every result links to the law or report page it came from, so you can check it yourself.

To begin, search Massachusetts law below by subject, citation or fund name, or scroll down to see the state as a whole. Select any law or fund to open its full record.

Massachusetts is the first state available. The Lab has coded penalty laws for seventeen more states; each will open here once its laws and financial reports are linked.

Release 1, November 14, 2026. Statutory text retrieved .

Search Massachusetts law and state funds

What do Confirmed, Under review, Lead and Not traced mean?
  • Confirmed. The law names the fund in its own words, and the law that creates the fund is still in force. You can rely on these links.
  • Under review. The destination was read from the law, or from the general rule that sends court fines to the state's General Fund. A Lab reviewer has not yet checked it.
  • Lead. The destination was reached through a reference to another law, or another law may send the money somewhere else. Treat it as a place to start looking.
  • Not traced. The law could not be found in the current code, or it contains no money language.

    Massachusetts as a whole

    These charts answer common questions about the state's laws before you look at any single law. Counts leave out repealed sections. The kinds of money and the recipients in each law were identified by reading each law's wording automatically and have not each been checked by hand, so open a law and read its text before you rely on it.

    Where in the law does money come up?

    How many sections in each Part of the General Laws mention each kind of money. Darker cells mean more sections. A section can mention several kinds.

    Do penalty laws say where their money goes?

    The 753 Massachusetts penalty laws in the Lab's Justice Funding Database, grouped by how the destination of their money is set. Bar colors show how certain each link is.

    Who does the law send money to?

    How many sections direct money to each kind of recipient.

    If a section names more than one kind of recipient, it is counted under each one.

    What do the funds that receive penalty money report?

    Money received each year (solid line) and the balance at year end (dashed line), fiscal years 2015 to 2025, from the state's annual Statutory Basis Financial Report. Each fund has its own scale. Select a fund to see its figures and the report pages they come from.

    These figures are each fund's totals from every source, so they do not tell you how much one law collected. A gap in a line means that year has not yet been read or its figures did not add up in the report. The General Fund is not shown here: at about $57.6 billion in FY2023, it is too large for fines inside it to be seen.

    Which subjects have the most penalty laws?

    The fifteen chapters with the most penalty laws. Select a chapter to list its laws.

    Do the law and the state's financial report agree?

    The 293 funds the state reported from FY2015 to FY2025, by whether each can be found in the General Laws under the same name.

    Where this information comes from

    Statutory text

    Massachusetts General Laws, retrieved from the Legislature's public data service on . Each provision links to its page on malegislature.gov. That site carries the Legislature's unofficial version; the Official Edition governs.

    Fund amounts

    Commonwealth of Massachusetts, Statutory Basis Financial Report, FY2015 to FY2025, Office of the Comptroller (macomptroller.org/sbfr). Each amount cites the report year and PDF page. Amounts are shown only where the report's own arithmetic checks hold.

    Penalties and links

    Justice Funding Database, Massachusetts, doi:10.7910/DVN/7RACQV. Statute-to-fund links: Yasin, Tauheeda, Massachusetts Statutes-to-Fund Linkages with Fiscal Amounts 2015–2025, doi:10.7910/DVN/LG1MZH.

    What it cannot tell you

    • How much money was actually collected or spent under a law.
    • Where a law sent its money in earlier years; links follow the law as it reads today.
    • Local government accounts; city and town figures will be added later.

    Justice Funding Database years are legislative session years. State fiscal years run July 1 to June 30 and are named for the year they end.
